application_type_full: Householder planning & demolition in a conservation area
description: Conversion of garage to habitable room; single storey rear extension; first floor side to rear extension; roof light in rear roof slope; lowering ground level towards rear garden; external alterations (Demolition of rear conservatory)
decision_conditions:
<p><span style="font-size:12.0pt;font-family:&quot;PT Sans&quot;,sans-serif;
mso-fareast-font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;mso-fareast-theme-font:minor-fareast;
mso-bidi-font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;mso-ansi-language:EN-GB;mso-fareast-language:
EN-GB;mso-bidi-language:AR-SA">The proposed first-floor side-to-rear extension,
by reason of its scale, siting and design, would diminish the characteristic
gap between buildings, create a harmful terracing effect, disrupt the symmetry
of the semi-detached pair and result in the loss of a prominent original
chimney. The proposal would therefore fail to preserve or enhance the character
or appearance of the Pinnerwood Park Conservation Area, causing less than
substantial harm to the significance of this designated heritage asset. No clear
and convincing justification or public benefits have been demonstrated that
would outweigh the identified harm. The proposal is therefore contrary to
Section 72(1) of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act
1990, paragraphs 212, 213 and 215 of the National Planning Policy Framework
(2024), Policy HC1 of the London Plan (2021), Policy HE1 of the Harrow
Development Management Policies Local Plan and the guidance contained within
the Pinnerwood Park Conservation Area Appraisal and Management Strategy.</span></p>
